reason: Conversation 1 stays on the safe side throughout: it asks the customer to clarify the display code against the model number, tells them not to open the casing, and recommends an engineer who tests inverter against magnetron. Conversation 2 gives prices in dollars at first, and its 'DIY Option' invites an inverter board swap on a high-voltage circuit, which is an unsupported and unsafe suggestion for a customer who has said they have no tools and won't open it. Conversation 2 also asserts specific UK repair price ranges and a rule about magnetron testing with more confidence than the situation supports. Both reach a similar repair-versus-replace conclusion, but Conversation 1 is safer and more honest about what only an engineer can determine.
